carousels.title: 5 myths that keep hotels addicted to OTAs

slides.headline: 5 myths that keep hotels addicted to OTAs
slides.sub: The stories that cost you six figures a year.

slides.title: “OTAs bring me guests I'd never reach.”
slides.body: 70% of OTA guests search your name directly afterward. You paid a finder's fee for a guest who already found you.

slides.title: “A direct site is too expensive to build.”
slides.body: One month of commission on a mid-size property often covers the entire build. It pays for itself, then keeps paying.

slides.title: “Guests trust Booking.com more than me.”
slides.body: Guests trust a fast, clear checkout — wherever it lives. Trust is a design problem, not a platform.

slides.title: “I can't compete under rate parity.”
slides.body: You don't compete on price. You compete on perks the OTA legally can't match: upgrades, late checkout, the real you.

slides.title: “Managing direct bookings is a headache.”
slides.body: With the right channel manager, direct is less work — one calendar, no disputes, no chargebacks you didn't cause.

slides.headline: Myths are expensive.
slides.sub: Math is cheap. We'll show you yours.

carousels.title: The performance budget we hold every build to

slides.headline: average hotel page load
slides.sub: Google's bar is 2.5. Here's the budget we hold every build to — and fail builds against.

slides.label: LARGEST CONTENTFUL PAINT
slides.note: How long until the biggest thing on screen actually appears. Google notices before your guest does.

slides.label: INTERACTION TO NEXT PAINT
slides.note: Date picker. Room filter. Guest count. A booking engine lives or dies on this one.

slides.title: The whole budget
items: LCP under 2.5 seconds
CLS under 0.1
INP under 200ms
Total blocking time under 200ms
First load under 2MB
HTML under 100KB compressed

slides.title: A budget is a number you can fail
slides.body: Anyone can promise “fast.” A budget is different — it's a gate. Miss one line and the build doesn't ship. That's the only version of this promise that means anything.

slides.headline: Want your numbers?
slides.sub: Send your URL. We'll run it against this exact budget and send back the failures.

carousels.title: Plugin sprawl is why your site is slow

slides.headline: Max 15 plugins. 25 on Elementor.
slides.sub: That's the rule. Here's why it's the rule.

slides.title: Not your host. Your plugins.
slides.body: Plugin sprawl is the single biggest cause of slow WordPress sites. Every one loads code on every page — including the three you installed once and forgot about.

slides.title: Audit each one against this
items: Does it run on every page, or one?
Does it add to time-to-first-byte?
Does it ship its own CSS and JavaScript?
Would removing it break anything a guest sees?

slides.label: THE COST OF ONE EXTRA SCRIPT
slides.note: Every chat widget, heatmap and pixel adds this to blocking time. Each one has to earn it.

slides.title: Audit quarterly, not never
slides.body: Plugin count only moves one direction unless somebody owns it. Put it on a calendar and it stops being a problem.

slides.headline: How many are you running?
slides.sub: Over 25 and we can almost tell you where your seconds went.

carousels.title: Five settings that quietly delete you from Google

slides.headline: 5 settings that quietly delete you from Google
slides.sub: We check every one before a build goes live. They cost minutes now and months later.

slides.title: “Discourage search engines” left on
slides.body: One checkbox under Settings → Reading. It survives launch more often than anyone admits, and the site simply never appears.

slides.title: robots.txt still says Disallow: /
slides.body: Copied over from staging with everything else. Every crawler obeys it, politely and completely.

slides.title: A noindex tag left by a staging plugin
slides.body: Invisible on the page. Fatal in the source. This is the one that takes weeks to notice.

carousels.title: OTA bookings cancel at twice the rate

slides.sub: Cancellation rate. Same rooms, different door.

slides.title: A cancelled booking is worse than no booking
slides.body: It blocked the room. It moved your pricing. And it hands you the same night to re-sell on short notice, at whatever rate you can still get.

slides.title: Commitment follows effort
slides.body: An OTA guest holds five tabs open and cancels four. A guest who found you, chose you, and booked on your own site has already decided.

slides.title: So direct isn't only cheaper
items: Cheaper — no commission
Steadier — half the cancellations
Yours — the guest data stays with you
